nodes.label: sequentially consistent
nodes.def: The strongest memory ordering requiring a single total order of all sequentially consistent operations visible to all threads; implied by default for std::atomic operations in C++.

nodes.label: c11 memory model
nodes.def: Standard C11 specification defining memory orderings: memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_consume, memory_order_acquire, memory_order_release, memory_order_acq_rel, memory_order_seq

nodes.label: exponential backoff
nodes.def: Contention management strategy backing off exponentially after failed lock acquisition; reduces bus traffic and collision; common in spinlock and CAS-based algorithm implementation

nodes.label: mcs lock
nodes.def: Queued lock where each waiting thread spins on a locally-owned node linked into a queue; cache-friendly with only O(1) bus traffic per lock acquisition; named after Mellor-Crummey

nodes.label: acquire semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all subsequent loads/stores cannot be reordered before the acquire operation; used for lock acquisition, reading a flag after volatile write.

nodes.label: happens before relation
nodes.def: A fundamental ordering relation in memory models defining that if operation A happens-before operation B, then A's effects are visible to B; forms the basis for reasoning about pro

nodes.label: synchronizes with
nodes.def: A relation between atomic operations in memory models where a release fence on one thread synchronizes with an acquire fence on another thread, establishing happens-before order ac

nodes.label: atomic cas
nodes.def: Compare-and-swap operation atomically loading a value, comparing it to an expected value, and storing a new value only if they matched, returning whether the swap occurred.

nodes.label: bounded buffer
nodes.def: Classic synchronization problem with fixed-size buffer between producers and consumers; requires empty/full conditions and mutual exclusion; solution uses semaphores or monitors.

nodes.label: current delay
nodes.def: The computed wait interval for the current retry iteration; derived from base_delay multiplied by backoff_multiplier raised to the iteration count, then capped by delay_ceiling.

nodes.label: deadlock
nodes.def: Liveness failure where two or more threads wait indefinitely for conditions held by each other; occurs with circular wait, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and mutual exclusion.

nodes.label: hardware transactional memory htm
nodes.def: CPU-supported transactional execution using cache hierarchies to track conflicts; Intel TSX and IBM Blue Gene/Q implementations; aborts on cache conflict or unsupported instruction

nodes.label: jitter
nodes.def: Randomized variance introduced into the computed delay to decorrelate competing threads and mitigate thundering-herd synchronization on lock release.

nodes.label: mcs lock enqueue
nodes.def: Operation appending a thread-local qnode to the queue tail; atomically CASes qnode into tail; on CAS failure, completes the predecessor's link and retries; ensures FIFO acquisition

nodes.label: memory barrier
nodes.def: Instruction or hardware mechanism that prevents reordering of memory operations across the barrier; ensures visibility and ordering of loads and stores relative to the barrier poin

nodes.label: release semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all prior loads/stores cannot be reordered after the release operation; used for lock release, writing data before a volatile flag.

nodes.label: spinlock
nodes.def: Lock implementation that spins in a tight loop waiting for acquisition; efficient when contention is brief but wasteful if held long; often implemented with atomic instructions.

nodes.label: atomic operation
nodes.def: Operation appearing indivisible to other threads; either hardware-supported single instruction atomics or software-implemented atomic primitives using CAS loops.

nodes.label: barrier synchronization
nodes.def: Primitive blocking threads until all threads in a set reach the barrier point; threads proceed only after the group is complete; used in fork-join and bulk-synchronous parallelism.

nodes.label: cache coherency
nodes.def: Protocol ensuring that multiple caches sharing a memory location present a consistent view; MESI, MOESI, MESIF protocols maintain coherence across CPU cores.

nodes.label: compare and swap cas
nodes.def: Atomic instruction comparing a value with expected and swaps only if equal; fundamental building block for lock-free algorithms; ABA problem may require additional solutions.

nodes.label: fork join parallelism
nodes.def: Parallelism pattern where work recursively splits into subtasks that join at barriers; implementations like Java ForkJoinFramework provide efficient work stealing for divide-conque

nodes.label: lock free
nodes.def: Progress guarantee where system-wide progress is always made; at least one thread completes an operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference.

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode
nodes.def: Thread-local queue node containing locked flag and successor pointer; must be cache-aligned and allocated per-thread to enable local spinning without shared contention.

nodes.label: mcs lock release
nodes.def: Operation by which a thread releases the lock; sets own qnode.locked to false to unblock spinning successor; if successor exists in qnode.next, responsibility transfers to successo

nodes.label: memory reclamation
nodes.def: Challenge of safely reclaiming freed memory in lock-free structures accessed concurrently; solutions include hazard pointers, RCU, epoch-based reclamation, and quiescent-state-base

nodes.label: mutex
nodes.def: Mutual exclusion primitive providing exclusive access to a resource; supports lock/unlock operations and optionally trylock; may be recursive or not; implements critical section se

nodes.def: Two-thread mutual exclusion algorithm using shared flags and a turn variable; provides bounded waiting under sequential consistency but fails on modern weak-memory hardware without

nodes.label: relaxed memory model
nodes.def: Memory model that permits more reorderings than sequential consistency; allows loads to be reordered with respect to stores, stores to be reordered with respect to stores, etc. Exa

nodes.label: semaphore
nodes.def: Synchronization primitive maintaining a counter representing available permits; P (wait/decrement) and V (signal/increment) operations; can control N concurrent accesses to a resou

nodes.label: sequential consistency
nodes.def: Memory model where all operations appear to execute in some total order consistent with program order on each thread; the default intuitive model where every load reads the result

nodes.label: total store order tso
nodes.def: Memory model used by x86/x64 processors where stores are globally ordered but may be buffered locally before becoming visible to other cores; a stronger model than ARM/PowerPC that

nodes.label: aba problem
nodes.def: Race condition in CAS-based algorithms where value changes from A to B and back to A between check and update, fooling CAS into succeeding incorrectly; solved with tagged pointers

nodes.label: atomic exchange
nodes.def: Atomic operation that reads the current value of a variable and writes a new value in a single indivisible step, returning the old value.

nodes.label: backoff iteration
nodes.def: Zero-based counter tracking how many consecutive failed lock acquisition attempts have occurred since last success.

nodes.label: backoff multiplier
nodes.def: Scaling factor (commonly 2.0) that multiplies the current delay on each failed acquisition attempt to produce the next delay interval.

nodes.label: base delay
nodes.def: Initial wait time in nanoseconds or microseconds before the first lock acquisition retry; the starting point of the exponential schedule.

nodes.label: cache line ping pong
nodes.def: Performance anti-pattern where threads on different cores repeatedly invalidate each other's cache line, causing excessive coherency traffic; often caused by false sharing or poorl

nodes.label: data race
nodes.def: Specific concurrent access where at least one access is a write, accesses are to same memory location, and accesses are not properly synchronized; undefined behavior in C11/C++11.

nodes.label: delay ceiling
nodes.def: Upper bound cap on the computed delay; prevents unbounded growth of wait times when contention persists across many iterations.

nodes.label: dining philosophers
nodes.def: Classic deadlock problem with N philosophers at circular table needing both adjacent forks; demonstrates resource ordering, deadlock avoidance, and starvation-free synchronization

nodes.label: hazard pointers
nodes.def: Memory reclamation technique where each thread publishes dangerous pointers to globally accessible locations; memory cannot be reclaimed while referenced by any hazard pointer.

nodes.label: lamport bakery algorithm
nodes.def: N-thread mutual exclusion algorithm providing first-come-first-served ordering; uses ticket numbers; correct under sequential consistency but requires adaptation for weak memory mo

nodes.label: mcs lock acquire
nodes.def: Operation by which a thread obtains the lock; spins polling its own qnode.locked field until false; returns only after predecessor has released and cleared the flag; no shared atom

nodes.label: mcs lock wait for successor
nodes.def: Sub-protocol when release finds no successor yet linked; thread performing release or a helper spins on qnode.next until non-null; ensures no lock holder exits before its successor

nodes.label: memory fence
nodes.def: Synonym for memory barrier; hardware instruction enforcing visibility and ordering constraints on memory operations across the fence; variations include full fence, store fence, lo

nodes.label: memory order acquire
nodes.def: Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores after the barrier in program order cannot be reordered before it, synchronizing with release stores.

nodes.label: mesi protocol
nodes.def: Four-state cache coherency protocol: Modified (exclusive, dirty), Exclusive (exclusive, clean), Shared (shared, clean), Invalid (not present); prevents inconsistent cached data.

nodes.label: monitor
nodes.def: High-level synchronization construct combining mutex and condition variables; object-oriented abstraction where methods acquire lock automatically; ensures serialized access to obj

nodes.label: out of order execution
nodes.def: CPU feature executing instructions in data-dependency order rather than program order; enables utilization of unused execution units; interacts with memory ordering guarantees.

nodes.label: priority inversion
nodes.def: Problem where low-priority thread blocks high-priority thread by holding a lock needed by both; typically resolved via priority inheritance protocols.

nodes.label: reader writer lock
nodes.def: Synchronization primitive allowing multiple concurrent readers or exclusive single writer; improves read-heavy workloads but has higher overhead than simple mutex.

nodes.label: readers writers problem
nodes.def: Synchronization problem requiring exclusive write access but concurrent read access; solutions vary in reader/writer preference, fairness, and implementation complexity.

nodes.label: relaxed atomicity guarantee
nodes.def: The sole guarantee provided by memory_order_relaxed: the atomic variable is read and written atomically without tearing, but no ordering constraints are imposed on other operations

nodes.label: reordering freedom privilege
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic operation imposes no constraints on the reordering of memory operations by either the compiler or the hardware; the operation may be reordered with any other opera

nodes.label: seq cst global total order
nodes.def: A single total order of all sequentially consistent operations that is visible and agreed upon by all threads in the system; the interleaving point where all threads observe the sa

nodes.label: seq cst synchronization protocol
nodes.def: The protocol by which sequentially consistent operations establish synchronization points between threads; creates a happens-before relationship across thread boundaries.

nodes.label: software transactional memory stm
nodes.def: Transactional memory implemented entirely in software; threads validate read sets and write sets; higher overhead than HTM but works on any hardware; examples: TL2, DSTM.

nodes.label: store buffering
nodes.def: Phenomenon where a store may be buffered and become visible later, allowing a subsequent load to observe a stale value while other threads see different orderings.

nodes.label: synchronizes with absence
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic operation does not synchronize with any other operation; it establishes no happens-before or synchronizes-with relationship with any thread, including the thread t

nodes.label: transactional memory
nodes.def: Concurrency control paradigm allowing sequences of operations to execute atomically without explicit locking; either hardware-assisted (HTM), software-only (STM), or hybrid.

nodes.label: amdahl law
nodes.def: Formula limiting parallel speedup by the serial fraction of computation; speedup <= 1 / (serial_fraction + parallel_fraction / num_threads); motivates minimization of synchronized

nodes.label: arm memory model
nodes.def: Weak memory model used by ARM processors where memory operations may be reordered extensively unless explicitly ordered by barriers; most permissive of common architectures.

nodes.label: atomic compare exchange
nodes.def: C++11/C11 atomic operation attempting to replace expected value with desired; returns boolean indicating success; on failure, expected is updated with actual value for retry loops.

nodes.label: binary semaphore
nodes.def: Semaphore with counter restricted to 0 or 1; functions like a mutex but without ownership semantics; can be signaled by non-owner thread.

nodes.label: bounded waiting
nodes.def: Property requiring that after a thread requests entry to a critical section, there is a bound on the number of other threads allowed to enter before the requester.

nodes.label: cache alignment
nodes.def: Placement of data structures on memory boundaries matching cache line size, typically 64 bytes, preventing false sharing between adjacent data.

nodes.label: causal consistency boundary
nodes.def: Relaxed operations respect intra-thread causality (program order) but do not guarantee inter-thread causality; this boundary defines the scope of what relaxed_atomicity guarantees.

nodes.label: channel csp
nodes.def: Communication primitive from Communicating Sequential Processes model; send and receive operations synchronize producers and consumers; implementations include Go channels, Clojure

nodes.label: clh lock
nodes.def: Queued lock using a linked list of nodes with spinning on predecessor's flag; provides scalability and fairness similar to MCS but different cache behavior.

nodes.label: coherence

nodes.label: compiler barrier
nodes.def: Directive preventing the compiler from reordering memory operations across the barrier; does not emit hardware instructions but prevents compiler optimization from causing races.

nodes.label: completable future
nodes.def: Java class implementing Future with completion callbacks, chaining, and composition; supports thenApply, thenCompose, exceptionally; enables non-blocking asynchronous pipelines.

nodes.label: condition variable
nodes.def: Primitive enabling a thread to wait for a condition to become true; must be used with a mutex; wait atomically releases the mutex and blocks; notify/notify_all wake waiting threads

nodes.label: context switch
nodes.def: Operating system operation saving one thread's state and restoring another's; involves kernel transition, register saves, TLB invalidation; cost motivates lock-free and per-thread

nodes.label: countdown latch
nodes.def: One-time barrier initialized with a count; threads decrement count on completion; barrier opens when count reaches zero; cannot be reused.

nodes.label: counting semaphore
nodes.def: General semaphore with non-negative integer counter allowing multiple concurrent accesses; used for resource pooling and bounded work distribution.

nodes.label: cpp11 memory model
nodes.def: C++11 and later standard library memory model supporting atomic operations with configurable ordering; provides std::atomic with memory_order enum values matching C11 semantics.

nodes.label: cross thread visibility non global
nodes.def: Other threads may observe relaxed operations in any order relative to each other; there is no single total order visible to all threads as there is with sequentially_consistent.

nodes.label: cyclic barrier
nodes.def: Barrier implementation that resets after all threads pass; supports configurable thread count and optional action executed when barrier breaks.

nodes.label: deadlock prevention
nodes.def: Design strategies eliminating one of the four Coffman conditions: no circular wait (lock ordering), hold-and-wait (acquire all at once), preemption (non-preemptive resources), mutu

nodes.label: decorrelated jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy where each thread computes delay = random.uniform(min_delay, previous_delay * 3); history-dependent decorrelation reduces coordinated retry waves.

nodes.label: dekker algorithm
nodes.def: First correct two-process mutual exclusion algorithm achieving progress under sequential consistency; combines turn-taking with turn variable; also fails under relaxed memory order

nodes.label: epoch based reclamation
nodes.def: Memory reclamation scheme batching deletions into epochs; threads must wait for active epochs to complete before reclaiming protected memory; balances throughput and safety.

nodes.label: equal jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy computing delay = base_delay / 2 + random.uniform(0, base_delay / 2); ensures wait never falls below half the nominal delay.

nodes.label: false sharing
nodes.def: Performance problem where unrelated variables sharing a cache line cause cache coherency traffic when one is modified; threads updating different variables contend due to line-leve

nodes.label: fetch and add
nodes.def: Atomic operation returning old value while atomically incrementing memory location; used for counters, ticket distribution, and implementing certain lock-free structures.

nodes.label: full jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy selecting a uniform random value in the range [0, current_delay]; maximizes desynchronization at the cost of potentially very short waits.

nodes.label: futex
nodes.def: Fast userspace mutex kernel-assisted synchronization; userspace spinning first, then syscall to kernel for wait/wake; basis for most Linux threading primitives.

nodes.label: future promise
nodes.def: Concurrency pattern decoupling value computation from access; Future represents pending result, Promise provides completion mechanism; enables asynchronous composition.

nodes.label: instruction reordering
nodes.def: CPU or compiler reordering of memory operations for performance while preserving single-thread correctness; can violate programmer expectations in concurrent code without proper ba

nodes.label: intra thread program order
nodes.def: Within a single thread, the thread still observes its own relaxed operations in program order; this total order is local to the thread and not shared.

nodes.label: invalidate queue
nodes.def: Hardware queue holding pending invalidation requests for cache lines; entries must be drained before a core can ensure it has exclusive ownership of a cache line.

nodes.label: linearizability
nodes.def: Correctness criterion requiring each operation appear to execute atomically at some point between invocation and response; composable property essential for concurrent object speci

nodes.label: livelock
nodes.def: Failure where threads continuously respond to each other without making progress; distinguishable from deadlock by active state; often result of excessive collision avoidance.

nodes.label: load buffering
nodes.def: Phenomenon in weak memory models where a load may observe a store from a different thread that happens later in global order, enabling patterns impossible under SC.

nodes.label: load linked store conditional
nodes.def: Pair of instructions for software atomic operations: LL reads atomically, SC writes only if no intervening store occurred; used on ARM, PowerPC; avoids ABA problem inherent to CAS.

nodes.label: lock elision

nodes.label: mcs lock fifo ordering
nodes.def: Property guaranteed by MCS queue structure; lock acquisition order matches the order of enqueue operations; provides fairness without centralized ticket counters.

nodes.label: mcs lock help links
nodes.def: Backoff resolution protocol during failed enqueue CAS; the thread that lost the CAS follows the discovered pointer chain to complete the linking work of the winner before retrying

nodes.label: mcs lock local spinning
nodes.def: Performance property of MCS; each waiter spins on its own thread-local qnode in its own cache line; eliminates cache-line ping-ponging between spinning threads; reduces bus traffic

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode locked
nodes.def: Boolean field in qnode; spinning thread reads this; set true on enqueue and cleared false by predecessor upon release; default true indicates lock not yet released.

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode next
nodes.def: Pointer field in qnode referencing successor qnode; null until predecessor links this node; spinning thread polls this to detect when it has been chained into the queue.

nodes.label: mcs lock tail
nodes.def: Atomic shared pointer to the last enqueued qnode; initialized null; updated via CAS during enqueue; represents the lock acquisition frontier.

nodes.def: C11/C++11 memory ordering that only guarantees atomicity of the operation with no ordering constraints relative to other operations; allows all reorderings.

nodes.label: memory order release
nodes.def: Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores before the barrier in program order cannot be reordered after it, making prior writes visible to acquiring threads.

nodes.label: mutex livelock prevention
nodes.def: Techniques including exponential backoff, random delays, or lock registry to prevent threads from repeatedly colliding on lock acquisition.

nodes.label: no happens before establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation neither participates in nor establishes a happens-before relationship with any other operation; operations may be reordered arbitrarily across thread boundaries

nodes.label: no synchronizes with establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation cannot synchronize-with any operation on another thread; release semantics and acquire semantics are absent, breaking the synchronizes-with chain.

nodes.label: numa awareness
nodes.def: Design consideration for systems with non-uniform memory access latency; thread affinity and data placement affect performance; synchronization must account for remote vs local mem

nodes.label: obstruction free
nodes.def: Progress guarantee where a thread completes an operation if it runs alone without interference; may starve under contention but has no blocking operations.

nodes.label: powerpc memory model
nodes.def: Weak memory model used by PowerPC/POWER processors with similar permissiveness to ARM; requires explicit barriers for many ordering guarantees.

nodes.label: priority inheritance
nodes.def: Protocol resolving priority inversion by temporarily elevating the priority of a lock-holding low-priority thread to match the highest blocked thread.

nodes.label: producer consumer
nodes.def: Concurrent pattern with producer threads generating work consumed by consumer threads; typically synchronized with bounded or unbounded channels/queues.

nodes.label: atomicity
nodes.def: The all-or-nothing property: a transaction's effects are either fully applied or fully absent; implemented via undo_log and transaction rollback.

nodes.label: isolation level
nodes.def: A configurable parameter defining the degree to which concurrent transactions are isolated from each other's uncommitted or intermediate effects.

nodes.label: rollback
nodes.def: The act of undoing a transaction's effects using undo_log entries, returning the database to its pre-transaction state.

nodes.label: tl log record
nodes.def: The fundamental unit of a transaction_log: a single append-only entry recording one atomic change or lifecycle event made by a transaction; identified by an lsn.

nodes.label: read committed
nodes.def: An isolation_level where each statement sees only data committed before that statement begins; prevents dirty_read but allows non_repeatable_read and phantom_read.

nodes.label: row level locking
nodes.def: Lock management at the individual row granularity via row_lock entries in lock_manager's lock table; enables high concurrency but increases lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: transaction state
nodes.def: The current phase of a transaction lifecycle: active, partially_committed, committed, aborted; drives lock release and recovery behavior.

nodes.label: acid properties
nodes.def: The four guarantees of database transactions: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — the foundational contract between a DBMS and its clients.

nodes.label: commit
nodes.def: The act of making a transaction's effects permanent: flush log records to durable storage, release locks, transition transaction_state to committed.

nodes.label: concurrency control
nodes.def: The set of mechanisms a DBMS uses to manage simultaneous access to shared data while preserving correctness and isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: database transaction
nodes.def: A logical unit of work executed against a database, bounded by BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK, guaranteeing ACID properties across one or more SQL operations.

nodes.label: dirty read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed; only possible in read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: commit visibility boundary
nodes.def: temporal threshold in read_committed: a datum is visible iff its committing_transaction committed before the reading statement started

nodes.label: committed data
nodes.def: database state resulting from successfully completed transactions; constitutes the visible universe for read_committed queries

nodes.label: exclusive lock
nodes.def: A lock type granting sole read-write access to a resource; incompatible with all other lock types including shared_lock and update_lock.

nodes.label: undo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the previous state of modified data; used to undo uncommitted transaction changes during rollback and recovery.

nodes.label: write ahead logging
nodes.def: A protocol requiring log records be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding data changes are applied; ensures durability and atomicity.

nodes.label: write lock held until commit
nodes.def: exclusive lock discipline in read_committed requiring a transaction to hold write locks on modified rows until transaction commit or rollback

nodes.label: before image
nodes.def: The committed database state of a row immediately before a transaction modifies it; recorded in the undo_log so the modification can be undone if the transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: committed
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after durable persistence of all changes; locks are released per locking_protocol rules.

nodes.label: lock granularity
nodes.def: The size of the database object protected by a lock: row_lock, page_lock, table_lock — trading off concurrency against lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: read uncommitted
nodes.def: The weakest isolation_level: transactions may observe uncommitted changes from other transactions, permitting dirty_read.

nodes.label: statement
nodes.def: A single SQL operation within a transaction; atomicity requires that each statement either fully completes its effect or fully reverts before the next statement begins.

nodes.label: statement level read consistency
nodes.def: guarantee within read_committed that each SQL statement sees all changes committed at the moment that statement began execution

nodes.label: tl checkpoint record
nodes.def: A special log_record written periodically by a checkpoint_writer; records the volatile database state at a consistent point, bounding the recovery_manager's replay horizon.

nodes.label: tl undo log
nodes.def: A structured collection of tl_update_record entries chained by a transaction; traversed in reverse order during rollback to restore the before_image of each modified entity.

nodes.label: tl update record
nodes.def: A log_record capturing a before_image and after_image of a modified data page or row; used by both redo_recovery (for durability) and undo_recovery (for atomicity rollback).

nodes.label: transaction boundary

nodes.label: transaction log
nodes.def: An append-only sequence of records tracking every change made by transactions; the primary mechanism for atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: two phase locking
nodes.def: A locking_protocol where transactions must acquire all locks during a growing_phase and release all locks during a shrinking_phase, guaranteeing conflict_serializable schedules.

nodes.label: uncommitted change
nodes.def: A modification to database state made by a transaction that has not yet committed; visible to other transactions at read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: aborted state
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after rollback completes; all acquired locks are released and the transaction cannot be restarted automatically.

nodes.label: all or nothing
nodes.def: The conceptual guarantee that a transaction executes as an indivisible unit: either every operation succeeds or no operation has any effect.

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A transaction transforms the database from one valid state to another, preserving all defined integrity constraints and business rules.

nodes.label: isolation
nodes.def: The property that concurrently executing transactions do not interfere with each other; the degree of interference is controlled by isolation_level.

nodes.label: lock timeout handling
nodes.def: timeout mechanism in read_committed for transactions blocked waiting to acquire conflicting locks on rows

nodes.label: locking protocol
nodes.def: A disciplined set of rules governing when locks may be acquired and released to ensure serializability or other isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: non repeatable read possible
nodes.def: the permitted anomaly in read_committed: a transaction reading the same row twice may observe different values if a concurrent transaction updates and commits that row between read

nodes.label: optimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that permits unrestricted execution and detects conflicts only at validation_phase, aborting and retrying on conflict.

nodes.label: serializable
nodes.def: The strongest isolation_level: the result of executing concurrent transactions is equivalent to some serial order of those transactions; prevents all anomalies.

nodes.label: statement start timestamp

nodes.label: strict two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where exclusive_locks are held until transaction end, ensuring strict_schedule and enabling cascading_less schedules.

nodes.label: timestamp ordering
nodes.def: A concurrency control method assigning timestamps to transactions and using them to order operations, ensuring serializability without locking.

nodes.label: tl abort record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction enters the aborted_state; signals that undo_log entries must be applied to reverse this transaction's effects.

nodes.label: tl checkpoint writer
nodes.def: The subsystem component that periodically writes a tl_checkpoint_record to the transaction_log; trims obsolete log segments and bounds crash_recovery time.

nodes.label: tl commit record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction commits; marks the durable persistence boundary for durability guarantees; flushed to disk before the transaction releases its locks.

nodes.def: A runtime data structure maintained by recovery_manager listing data pages modified but not yet flushed; consulted during checkpoint to ensure write_ahead_logging invariants hold.

nodes.label: transaction read
nodes.def: The act of a transaction executing a read operation; at read_uncommitted this read may return uncommitted_change from concurrent transactions.

nodes.label: update lock
nodes.def: A lock type that prevents deadlock during lock_upgrade: compatible with shared_lock but not with other update_locks or exclusive_locks.

nodes.label: write lock not required
nodes.def: The characteristic of read_uncommitted where a writing transaction does not hold an exclusive lock preventing other transactions from reading its uncommitted state.

nodes.label: active state

nodes.label: pt08

nodes.label: type error

nodes.label: type scheme

nodes.label: monotype

nodes.label: most general unifier
nodes.def: Most general substitution that satisfies a set of type constraints; unique up to renaming of variables.

nodes.label: null safety

nodes.label: prism builder
nodes.def: A constructor taking a du_payload and injecting it as the sole du_variant under a specific du_tag, rebuilding the sum type from the selected summand.

nodes.label: prism matcher
nodes.def: A partial function over a sum type that succeeds only when the active du_tag matches the target, yielding the contained du_payload; otherwise the sum is preserved.

nodes.label: pt01
nodes.def: principal_type: the unique most-general type that captures all valid typings for an expression, serving as the output of type inference

nodes.label: pt04
nodes.def: unification: the algorithm that finds the most general substitution making two types equal, central to constraint solving in inference

nodes.label: pt05
nodes.def: substitution: a mapping from type variables to types that, when applied, resolves all variables in a type expression

nodes.label: pt11
nodes.def: let_polymorphism: the polymorphism arising from let-bindings where the bound expression is generalized, giving it a principal type scheme

nodes.label: record type

nodes.label: type annotation
nodes.def: Explicit syntactic marker associating a name or expression with a type (e.g. x: int).

nodes.label: array type
nodes.def: Homogeneous mutable sequence with element type (list[int] in Python).

nodes.label: bidirectional type inference
nodes.def: A mode of type_inference splitting into two directions: synthesize (produce a type from an expression alone) and check (verify an expression against a given expected_type), compose

nodes.label: borrowing
nodes.def: Temporary access to data without taking ownership, with borrow checker enforcement.

nodes.label: boxing
nodes.def: Wrapping primitive value in heap-allocated object wrapper (int → Integer).

nodes.label: collection type
nodes.def: Generic container type (List[T], Set[T], Map[K,V]) with element type parameter.

nodes.label: ct bound variable
nodes.def: A type variable bound by a ∀ quantifier in a type scheme; subject to instantiation.

nodes.label: dependent type
nodes.def: Type that depends on a runtime value, enabling compile-time proofs about data.

nodes.label: du primitive
nodes.def: An untagged union of types without a du_tag. The discriminated union adds a tag to this primitive structure to make variant membership verifiable.

nodes.label: exhaustive check
nodes.def: Compiler verification that all cases of a union are handled in pattern matching.

nodes.label: existential type
nodes.def: Abstraction hiding a type (some T such that property holds) from consumers.

nodes.label: free type variables
nodes.def: Set of type variables occurring in a type that are not quantified; relevant to generalization.

nodes.label: generic type
nodes.def: Type or function parameterized by one or more type variables enabling code reuse across types.

nodes.label: higher kinded type
nodes.def: Type constructor taking another type as argument (Functor[F[_]] in Scala).

nodes.label: invariance
nodes.def: Generic has no subtyping relationship regardless of component types (mutable container).

nodes.label: lens getter

nodes.label: lens setter

nodes.label: narrowing

nodes.label: occurs check

nodes.label: optic law set set

nodes.label: ownership

nodes.label: parametric polymorphism
nodes.def: Same implementation works uniformly over a range of types via type parameters.

nodes.label: phantom type

nodes.label: polytype

nodes.label: principal pair

nodes.label: type family

nodes.label: type parameter

nodes.label: type safe union

nodes.label: variance

nodes.label: compound type

nodes.label: conditional type
